title: T709-903GA SELF-HEALING ARCHITECTURES FOR CYBER RESILIENT GROUND SEGMENT SYSTEMS (EXPRO+)
description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

title: ARTES 4.0 STRATEGIC PROGRAMME LINE OPTICAL COMMUNICATION SCYLIGHT ROLLING WORK PLAN FOR 2020 - 2021
description: 1. Introduction: The work plan was established based on an ESA internal "ARTES ScyLight Call for Ideas" and reflects the findings from industry workshops or the consolidation process with stakeholders, like National Delegations, operators, service providers, satellite manufacturers, industry and experts. In addition, the work plan lists activities inherited from the former ARTES ScyLight Element work plans that will be issued under the new legal framework of the ARTES 4.0 Strategic Programme Line (SPL) "Optical Communication - ScyLight". 2.Strategic Activities: A number of activities are identified as of immediate strategic importance as they supportadvancement of optical communications technologies, e.g. towards the "fibre in the sky" vision, or they address system relevant elements. Some of those activities have been addressed in ITTs under the legacy ScyLight Element, but have not resulted in contracts, due to lack of overall budget within the Participating States' allocations. However, those activities are still considered of high strategic value and are listed again (or slightly modified) in the proposed work plan. Furthermore, the SPL Optical Communication - ScyLight is supposed to evaluate the benefits of optical communications in more general terms, also beyond pure near Earth satcom applications. Lastly, ScyLight is aiming to foster the maturity of the industrial landscape in Europe/Canada to prepare for future upcoming markets. Some of those strategic areas are listed below.- Foster Industrial Landscape- Atmospheric Effects- Optical Communication Terminal Technologies- High Data Rate and RF/Optical Coupling- Quantum Communications- Standardisation3. Implementation: Thefollowing implementation philosophy will be followed: Phasing: phasing of the contractual activities may be considered, depending on the risks associated with the development, the maturity of the technologies, and potential early market perspectives. ParallelContracts: in accordance with the ARTES 4.0 Implementing Rules, parallel contracts may be awarded. Procurement Policy: the following procurement policies are foreseen for the proposed activities:C: Activities in open competition without any further restrictions. C1:Activities in open competition limited to non-Large System Integrators (LSIs) as prime. LSIs are allowed to participate as sub-contractors.C2: Activities are in open competition, where a significant participation of non-LSIs is requested.C3: Activity restrictedto SMEs RD organisations, preferably in cooperation.C4: Activities in open competition, subject to the SME subcontractingclause.Implementation Category (formerly "Priority"): the activities comprising the SPL Optical Communication - ScyLight Work Planhave been designated as either B (Baseline) - formerly P1, or R (at the Request of delegates). The assignment of activities to these categories is not a declaration of technological, commercial or programmatic priority; instead, it simply indicates whether an activity requires a prior request from a Delegation for the ITT to be generated and released. ITTs for activities designated priority B will automatically be generated by the Executive. The planned ITT issue dates are indicated in Annex II; however, baseline activities for which industry and/or Delegations declare an interest will be implemented as a priority. Such interest can be notified directly to the ARTES ScyLight Programme Office. title: EXPRO + NAVISP ELEMENT 1 (NAVISP-EL1-015): FEASIBILITY STUDY OF A SPACE-BASED RELATIVISTIC PNT SYSTEM
description: This EXPRO+ procurement is part of the NAVISP Programme, under Elelment 1, Work Plan 2018.All GNSS in operation at present are based on Newtonian physics and rely on global reference frames fixed to Earth. Relativistic effects are treated as deviations that need to be corrected for. Precision and stability in time of the reference frames is provided via ground stations and they are limitedby the Earths dynamics and atmosphere. Several theoretical concepts have been proposed for the use of Relativistic Positioning Systems (RPS) and the required relativistic reference frames. These have been studied with different approaches during the last years and the consistency with the General Relativity has been demonstrated. However, none of the proposed approaches were intended to be practical. The proposed activity will address the maturity of RPS for timing and positioning applications, the definition of a consolidated concept and architecture for a RPS constellation suitable for navigation both in the Earth surface and the near-Earth Space,and the High Level Requirements for a proof-of-concept based on current and near-future available state of the art technology.
